memory_candidates.content: sync-manifest-scripts.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/) diffs a new script's presence against `git ls-files`, not a raw disk walk -- an untracked new file is invisible to both --check and --write until it is `git add`-ed. Add new scripts before invoking this script, not after.

When writing a text-level bash lint that classifies a guard idiom as mandatory-vs-optional by scanning forward for an exit/return signal, scope the scan to the specific if-branch's own body (bounded by the next elif/else/fi), never a blind N-line window: a blind window can pull in a semantically unrelated exit from a nested, unrelated else-branch (measured: deploy-freshness-lib.sh's staleness-refusal exit nested inside an 'optional library found' else-branch), and must separately skip comment lines, since prose describing an exit code inline (e.g. documenting a bash quirk) can textually match the same signal regex.

sapience_notes.subject: sync-manifest-scripts.sh
sapience_notes.value: Diffs a new script's presence against `git ls-files`, not a raw disk walk. An untracked new script under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ is invisible to both --check and --write until it has been `git add`-ed.

sapience_notes.subject: generate-context-line-counts.sh
sapience_notes.value: Refuses to run from the agent-system source store (a deploy-root-guard.sh-style guard); it only runs against a deployed .claude/scripts (or .opencode/scripts) tree. A source-store-only edit to a context file must have its index-entries.json line_count applied by hand (a plain wc -l) until a redeploy makes the real script runnable, at which point --check should confirm the hand-applied value was exact.

sapience_notes.subject: lint-fixture-dependency-declaration.sh
sapience_notes.value: New verify-deploy.sh gate 30: detects a scripts/tests/*.sh fixture suite whose declared/copied sandbox set omits a mandatory scripts/lib/*.sh dependency of a script it copies. Classifies each lib/*.sh guard occurrence into one of four shapes (unconditional hard-fail, degrade-safe single-line guard, search-loop log-and-continue pass-through, lazy fail-closed-on-first-use function wrapper), and deliberately never flags the fourth shape at all since static text analysis cannot determine whether a given suite's own scenarios reach the CLI subcommand that triggers it.

sapience_notes.subject: update-task-status.sh's hb_lib / phase-heartbeat-lib.sh guard (update-phase-status.sh)
sapience_notes.value: A bare `if [[ -n "$VAR" ]]; then . "$VAR"; fi` with no error branch at all (no echo, no exit) is a legitimate, even-more-silent degrade-safe optional-dependency shape beyond the three the original drift-lint research enumerated (single-line [ -f ] && guard; search-loop log-and-continue; lazy fail-closed function wrapper).

sapience_notes.subject: update-task-status.sh's OVERLAP_LIB/FRESHNESS_LIB guard
sapience_notes.value: The 'library found' else-branch of this degrade-safe search-loop guard nests a semantically unrelated hard exit (exit 6, the deploy-staleness refusal) two levels deep inside further nested ifs. A classifier must never treat 'any exit/return found anywhere forward of the guard' as proof the guard itself is mandatory -- it must scope strictly to the guard's own first (not-found) branch.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-deploy.sh gate timeouts on this host
sapience_notes.value: Gates with a 60s budget (gate 3 doc-lint, gate 4 task-reference lint) can transiently time out when deploy-headless.sh's own internal fast-gate pass runs under a measured host load average of ~9; a standalone re-run of the same gates passes cleanly within ~42s. Treat a lone 60s-budget timeout during a concurrent deploy pass as a host-contention signal to re-check standalone before treating it as a regression.
